header.name: Introduction to Nanoelectronics
header.description: Nanoelectronics is an interdisciplinary area of research which has a huge potential and is currently attracting a great deal of attention. The objective of this course is to understand the basic principles that govern the operation and electrical characteristics of nanoelectronic devices and become familiar with the recent research being undertaken in nanoelectronics.
prerequisites_mandatory: Physics of Semiconductor Devices (UG) and equivalent for PG
prerequisites_mandatory_resolved: Physics of Semiconductor Devices (UG) and equivalent for PG

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Clearly explains distinct phenomena that are important in nanoelectronic devices.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Is able to describe electron transport in low-dimensional materials and the theoretical frameworks of nanoelectronic devices.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Is able to analyze spin transport, spintronic and non-classical electronic devices.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Is able to identify the applications of nanoelectronic and spintronic devices in logic/memory and other related applications

lecture_topics: Overview of Nanoelectronics: significance, "bottom-up" approach to build devices, trends and IRDS perspective
Introduction to Quantum Mechanics: Schrodinger’s equation, quantum confined systems
Quantum Phenomena: Tunnelling effect, WKB approximation, direct and indirect tunnelling, coherent and incoherent tunnelling, tunelling devices
Electronic nature of nanomaterials: Energy bands and carrier densities in quantum well, quantum wire and quantum dot
Current flow: Transport in confined materials, ballistic transport, quantum resistance and conductance, Landauer Buttiker formalism
Nanotransistor: Output and transfer characteristics, subthreshold swing, limits on subthreshold swing and its consequences, quantum capacitance
Advanced materials for nanotransistors: 2D, 1D, and 0D transistors, Coulomb blockade in nanotransistors, advantages and challenges.
Spin transport: Overview of spin electronics, materials for spin electronics, spin polarizers and analyzers, spin injection, detection and relaxation
Spin transport: Spin-polarized transport, spin filtering effect, spin Seebeck and magneto-caloric effect, spin Hall and inverse spin Hall effect, spin Nernst effect
Spin dynamics: spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, LLG equation, magnetic anisotropies, skyrmions, spin torque effect
Spintronic devices: Theory of magnetoresistances (AMR, GMR, TMR), magnetic tunnel junctions, Datta-Das spin transistor
Spintronic device applications: Emerging spintronic memories (STT-, SOT-, ME-, DW-MRAM, etc.), magneto-logic gates (magnetic AND, OR, NAND, NOR, etc.), advantages and challenges.
